Here's what I found regarding the ruff parser's re-lexing logic, f-string error recovery, and unclosed brace handling:

## The Core Problem

The original issue (#11916) laid out the challenge: there's more to f-strings than a normal string literal because it can contain an expression element. This means that there could be unterminated f-string or the closing curly brace could be missing or an error in the expression itself.

At the time, the parser dropped all unterminated strings—more precisely, the lexer didn't emit the string token for unterminated strings. This was true for both normal and formatted string literals.

The proposed fix involved re-lexing: because of an unclosed `{`, there's a NonLogicalNewline token after the variable. This would require a modified re-lexing logic to (1) recover from an unclosed `{` and (2) recover from an unterminated f-string. This also requires moving the error handling from the lexer to the parser.

A key related concern was list parsing: the parser didn't use existing list parsing logic for parsing comma-separated expressions (tuple expressions), which meant it didn't benefit from error recovery logic. Thus, if there was an error in the f-string expression itself, there was a high chance it wouldn't recover correctly.

## The Re-lexing PR (#11845)

The foundational re-lexing work by dhruvmanila: This PR implements the re-lexing logic in the parser. This logic is only applied when recovering from an error during list parsing.

## The `parse_list` / `unreachable` Panic (PR #19183)

A directly relevant fix by dylwil3 addressed a panic tied to `parse_list` recovery and TStringMiddle. The parser begins parsing the f-string and expects to see a list of objects, essentially alternating between interpolated elements and ordinary strings. It is happy to see the first left brace, but then there is a lexical error.

The recovery failure mechanism: when the parser sees the TStringStart, error recovery says "that's a list element I don't know what to do with, let's skip it." When it sees TStringMiddle it tries to parse it as one of the literal elements of the FString. Unfortunately, the function being used to parse individual list elements thinks it's not possible to have a TStringMiddle sitting in the FString, and hits unreachable.

## The Most Recent Fix (PR #20848)

The latest improvement by MichaReiser preserves tokens rather than converting them: This PR improves the lexer to preserve STRING tokens instead of converting them to Unknown if a string literal misses its closing quotes. Instead of converting to UNKNOWN, it sets a flag on the string literal that allows upstream tools to check if it's an unclosed string literal. The benefit is much better error recovery because the parser now recognizes those literals.

This regressed and then re-fixed f-string handling specifically: preserving the kind for unclosed string literals regressed the f-string's and t-string's recovery mechanism, so it was improved too—preserving the F-STRING middle even if it's unclosed (e.g. `f"unclosed`), with better recovery for missing `}`. The parser now matches the quotes for `f"{ab"` instead of assuming that the closing quotes start a new string.

The specific `"f-string: unterminated string"` error message you referenced appears in older issues like #5044, where ruff failed to handle a valid f-string with escaped braces, producing "Failed to parse... f-string: unterminated string." The chain of PRs above (#11845 → #19183 → #20848) progressively moved error handling out of the lexer into the parser, made f-string expression parsing use `parse_list` recovery, and preserved unclosed tokens for cleaner recovery.

## The Core Re-lexing Implementation (PR #11845)

The foundational work was this PR implements the re-lexing logic in the parser. This logic is only applied when recovering from an error during list parsing. The logic is as follows: During list parsing, if an unexpected token is encountered and it detects that an outer context can understand it and thus recover from it, it invokes the re-lexing logic in the lexer. This logic first checks if the lexer is in a parenthesized context and returns if it's not.

The mechanism works by reducing nesting levels: it then reduces the nesting level by 1. It shouldn't reset it to 0 because otherwise the recovery from nested list parsing will be incorrect. Then, it tries to find last newline character going backwards from the current position of the lexer. This avoids any whitespaces but if it encounters any character other than newline or whitespace, it aborts.

## F-string Error Recovery in List Parsing (Issue #11946)

This issue identified problems with the re-lexing approach in parenthesized contexts. The re-lexing will reduce the nesting level when recovering from an unclosed f-string but the lexer isn't in an expression element so the nesting level it reduced is the one from the outer context. This means that it'll emit an Indent token before param2 which is incorrect.

A second scenario involved format specifiers: the parser uses the same list parsing logic for parsing both the outer f-string elements and the ones in the format specifier. This means that when it tries to recover from an unclosed f-string, it reduces the nesting level twice (1) when re-lexing from the format spec and (2) when re-lexing from the outer f-string.

The proposed solution was to reduce the nesting level only if the parser is recovering from within an expression element of an f-string (fstring.is_in_expression) and avoid calling into re-lexing when recovering from the format specifier.

## Line Continuation Bug Fix (PR #12008)

A related fix addressed the logical newline recovery: this PR fixes a bug where the re-lexing logic didn't consider the line continuation character being present before the newline character. This meant that the lexer was being moved back to the newline character which is actually ignored via \.

## Related Follow-up Issue (#12036)

Another edge case involved comments: even with the fix in #12035, we still need to consider the fact that the line continuation character could be part of the comment which means that the newline character is not being escaped. This won't create a panic but the lexer won't be moved back and keep the NonLogicalNewline token instead of changing it to Newline token.

The suggested fix was to update TokenSource to pass in the last comment token range to re-lexing method on the lexer which can be used to check if this line continuation is part of the comment or not.

This task reconstructs upstream Ruff **PR #11871 – "Use re-lexing for normal list parsing"**, which improves error recovery for f-strings with syntax errors. I confirmed the repo sits exactly at that PR's base commit (matching `mod.rs`, and all four affected snapshots), so every task bullet maps to this single PR — whose only source change is in `parser/mod.rs`.

### Changes made (source/resource only — `tests/` untouched)

1. **`crates/ruff_python_parser/src/parser/mod.rs`** — Updated the `parse_list` recovery loop to mirror `parse_comma_separated_list`:
   - Use `is_regular_list_terminator` instead of `is_list_terminator`.
   - When an unrecognized token is an element/terminator of an *enclosing* list, re-lex it as a logical-line token (`self.tokens.re_lex_logical_token()`) and break out — **before** emitting any error.
